title: Player
description: What the player's own body looks like. A content type with exactly one entry, and it exists because the player is the one body in the world that carries no content id of its own: a zombie hands over its type id, a unique survivor its identity id, a raider its archetype id, and the player -- who is none of those -- had nothing to resolve a look from, so `Appearance.for_entity` never found a sprite for it and the shipped game had no player art at all. `presentation/appearance.gd`'s PLAYER_LOOK_ID is the one place that names the id below, so the draw loop still carries no `if id ==` branch. Deliberately NOT an entry under survivors/: survivor.schema.json pins ids to ^survivor\.unique\. (the frozen TypeScript oracle validates that with Ajv and would refuse a player id), and SimSurvivors.list_uniques boots everything under survivors/ -- an entry there would spawn a phantom NPC. NOTE: the content validator is shallow -- top-level types and unexpected top-level keys only -- and does not recurse into `appearance`; check_appearance.gd is the gate that checks the block's inner shape, and check_topdown.gd is the one that proves the draw loop reads it. The oracle knows six content directories and players/ is not one of them, so this schema is read by content_validator.gd alone.

id.description: Stable namespaced id, always player.<thing>. One entry ships -- player.body -- and the namespace is open because the rig is not necessarily the only thing about the player that content will come to decide.

name.description: Human-readable name. Never shown to the player: the HUD speaks in prose from sim read models, and this is for whoever is reading the content.

appearance.description: The same block a zombie or a survivor carries. `sprite` is required here, unlike on a pawn: the whole point of this type is that the player has art, and an entry declaring only a tint would leave the body a coloured disc while claiming to have fixed that.

hitFx.description: The effect sheet a blow drawn on this body plays where it lands (docs/23, 'The shot is seen'): an authored `sheet` family in godot/assets/sprites/authored.json, played by presentation/fx_look.gd on `attack.connected` and `bite.landed` when the player sees the body. One picture for every blow -- a scratch, a bite, a graze and a killing shot draw the identical frames, because the sheet is chosen by who was struck and never by what struck them or how hard (docs/01 clause 4: a bite can present as a scratch).

sprite.description: Registry key for assets/sprites/<key>.png, feet-anchored on the pawn canvas (one ART_NATIVE tile wide by one and a quarter tall, 32x40; presentation/appearance.gd's PAWN_KEYS, assets/sprites/README.md). Drawn face-on and mirrored when the body faces west; nobody rotates, the player included.

tint.description: Optional, and absent on the shipped entry: finished art draws as painted and a declared tint would multiply every pixel of it (Appearance.modulate_for). Palette's `player` colour is the fallback when this content is missing entirely, not a tint.

corpseSprites.description: Settled corpse pictures. Presentation selects one stably per entity and draws it at its ground anchor only after death.

outfit.description: What a body on this rig wears in a slot it has nothing equipped in, so nobody is drawn in the pack survivor's underwear (docs/23, 'Clothe everyone'). Each slot lists garment families -- authored.json kind `wear`, painted per frame onto the pack survivor -- and presentation/appearance.gd's `outfit_of` picks one per body by its full entity id, with no simulation random draw: a cosmetic default, never an item, so it weighs nothing, warms nothing and is not in any inventory. An item equipped in the slot replaces it with the item's own `appearance.equipSprite`. Every body on the `body_survivor` rig without an outfit of its own falls back to this one, the way human corpses fall back to this entry's `corpseSprites`.
